messages.text: My watchx takes a long time to charge, it recently took 2-3 days to go to 100%
Searched the web · WatchX DePIN watch charging slow

I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Let's work out why your WatchX is charging so slowly.

Taking 2 to 3 days to reach 100% isn't normal, so something is off. Most of the time it's the charger connection, not the watch.

First, can you tell me two things?

1. Which WatchX do you have: the Fusion or the Founder edition?
2. What is the charging cable plugged into: a laptop or PC USB port, a power bank, or a USB wall adapter?

While you check, try this:

1. Wipe the metal charging pins on the back of the watch and on the cable with a dry cloth or a cotton swab. Sweat and skin oil build up on them and can stop a good contact.
2. Put the watch on the charger and make sure it snaps on firmly and sits flat. If it's crooked or loose, it can charge very slowly or keep starting and stopping.
3. Plug the cable into a plain USB wall adapter instead of a computer port.

After that, let me know whether the screen shows the charging symbol and how much the battery goes up in about 30 minutes.
Fusion, plugged into a USB charger, it shows charging but then the display goes dark like the battery is dead and stats like that till fully charged

Thanks, that helps. The screen going dark on the charger could be normal: the Fusion has an AMOLED screen, and like most smartwatches it may just switch the display off to save power while it keeps charging. Or the watch could actually be shutting down. Let's find out which.

Next check:

1. Put the watch on the USB charger and wait until the screen goes dark.
2. Press the side button once, or tap the screen.
3. Let me know what happens:
   - The screen wakes and shows a battery percentage (please tell me the number)
   - It shows only the charging symbol or an empty battery
   - Nothing happens at all
4. If it wakes, wait about 30 minutes, wake it again and tell me the new percentage.

That will tell us whether it's charging slowly or stopping and starting.
I had it charged to 65% but when I removed it from the charger it dropped to 35% I last out it on the charger at 4% and it still showed 4% after a couple hours

Thanks, those numbers tell us a lot.

A drop from 65% to 35% the moment it comes off the charger, and being stuck at 4% for hours on it, isn't a settings problem. It means one of two things:

- **The charge isn't getting through properly.** Bad contact at the pins, or a weak cable or adapter. The watch shows a "charging" reading that isn't real.
- **The battery itself is worn.** It can't hold its voltage, so the percentage drops sharply once the charger is removed.

Let's rule out the charging side first:

1. Plug the watch's cable into a different USB wall adapter, like a phone charger you know works, and a different outlet.
2. Look closely at the metal pins on the back of the watch and on the cable end. Check for dark spots, green or white crust, or a pin that sits lower than the others.
3. Leave it charging for 1 hour, then take it off and tell me:
   - The percentage just before you removed it
   - The percentage 5 minutes after

If you can, please also send a close-up photo of the pins on the watch and on the cable.
After 1 hour it went from 35% to 36% stayed at 36% after 5 minutes
Handed to the team · Software and settings ruled out. It is either the magnetic charging cable/contac

Thanks for testing that. Gaining only 1% in an hour means the watch is barely taking any charge. The adapter doesn't seem to be the problem, so it's down to one of two things:

- **The charging cable or its contacts.** The magnetic charger isn't passing enough current through.
- **The watch's battery or charging circuit.** That would explain the drop from 65% to 35% when you unplugged it.

I can't tell which from here, so I've passed everything we tested to JD, our hardware lead. The team is offline right now. They'll pick it up tomorrow at 10am ET, and the answer will come to your email.

Two things would help JD:

1. **A close-up photo of the pins** on the back of the watch and on the cable end, sent here in the chat.
2. **Another WatchX charging cable, if you can borrow one.** Charge with it for an hour and let me know whether you get more than 1%. That tells us right away whether it's the cable or the watch.

If you'd like a quicker answer, the community and JD are very active on our Discord: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf . Post your results and mention @nullhashrate.
